recommendation: Keep the audit as-is. If future package validation shows hl7.fhir.r6.search is missing these instances, investigate publisher/package-generation tooling; no core source edit is indicated by the current source and history.
issue_request: FHIR-39010 was a Published FHIR-I change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5, asking that generated output artifacts include individual/resource-specific SearchParameter definitions in addition to the combined search parameters used in the rendered registry.
initial_application: The Jira-tagged application commit a4ed0ed8 added an hl7.fhir.r5.search package entry to source/downloads.html describing a package where combined search parameters are uncombined into a set of search parameters for each resource. The current source contains per-resource bundle-<Resource>-search-params.xml files, including Patient-specific definitions derived from combined/common definitions.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes asked for clarification on 2023-01-09 and then approved FHIR-39010 Persuasive with Modification by Grahame Grieve/Gino Canessa 13-0-0 on 2023-01-30. The Jira resolution says the resource-specific instances should be in published packages for R5 and later, should not show up in the rendered spec, and should not be referenced by CapabilityStatements. A November 2022 Zulip implementers thread supports interpreting individual search parameters as package content rather than separate rendered pages.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current build-scoped downloads page lists hl7.fhir.r6.search.tgz as the search-parameter package with uncombined/resource-specific entries, and active resource folders contain per-resource search-parameter bundle source files. Adding rendered registry links or CapabilityStatement references would conflict with the issue resolution.

evidence_items.learned: This establishes that package content, not additional rendered registry pages, is the approved target behavior.
